headline: GOLD NEARS $4,750 AS IRAN PEACE DEAL HOPES CRASH OIL — Silver Tests $80, Rate Cut Bets Surge
snippet: Spot gold climbed to a two-week high of $4,735/oz on May 7 as hopes for a US-Iran peace memorandum sent oil prices tumbling, easing inflation expectations and triggering a surge in rate-cut bets; silver outperformed with a 3.4% gain to near $80/oz.

headline: NSW LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL VOTES TO SCRAP 40-YEAR URANIUM BAN — Australia's Largest State Opens Up
snippet: Australia's NSW Legislative Council voted 21–19 on May 7 to pass a bill repealing the state's 40-year uranium mining ban, clearing the upper house despite Labor and Greens opposition; the legislation still requires the Assembly's approval before the prohibition is formally lifted.

headline: SIX STRAIGHT YEARS: Silver Deficit Has Drained 762 Million Oz From Global Stockpiles — A Full Year of Mine Output Gone
snippet: The Silver Institute's 2026 World Silver Survey confirmed a sixth consecutive structural deficit, with 762 million ounces pulled from global inventories since 2021 — equivalent to an entire year of world mine production — as solar, EV, and investment demand continues to overwhelm supply.

headline: OPINION: Iran Is the Trigger, But the Fed Is What's Really Moving Gold and Silver Right Now
snippet: GoldSilver.com argues the real mechanism behind gold's move above $4,700 is not a safe-haven bid — a Hormuz reopening lowers oil, cools PCE inflation, and compels the Fed to cut rates, with compressed real yields being the engine behind every major gold rally since 2020.

headline: B2GOLD DOUBLES REVENUE to $1.16B in Q1 — Goose Mine Fire Cuts Q2 Output 35%, Full-Year Guidance Intact
snippet: B2Gold (TSX: BTO) reported Q1 gold revenue of $1.16B and net income of $205M, both more than doubling year-over-year on record gold prices; Q2 Goose Mine output guidance was cut roughly 35% to 18,000–20,000 oz after an April 16 crushing circuit fire in Nunavut, though full-year guidance of 170,000–230,000 oz was reaffirmed.

headline: RARE EARTHS AMERICAS Closes $63.3M Upsized IPO on NYSE — Targets NdPr, Dysprosium and Terbium in Brazil and Georgia
snippet: Rare Earths Americas (NYSE American: REA) closed a $63.3M upsized IPO at $19/share — the top of its range — on May 6, popping 32% at the open before closing flat on its debut; the exploration-stage company targets neodymium-praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium from heavy rare earth projects in Georgia and Brazil.

headline: CHILE LITHIUM EXPORTS SURGE 175% in April as SQM-Codelco Partnership Ramps — Copper Barely Moves
snippet: Chile's April 2026 exports rose 7% to $9.7B, with lithium carbonate surging 175% to $498M as the SQM-Codelco partnership scales toward 300,000 tonnes of annual production; copper grew just 0.3% on falling concentrate volumes, its weakest monthly performance since March 2024.

headline: COPPER EYES 3% WEEKLY GAIN as Iran Peace Hopes Ease Inflation Fears — Sulphuric Acid Supply Risk Lingers
snippet: Copper futures held above $6.10/lb on May 8 and were tracking a 3%+ weekly gain as Iran peace deal hopes eased oil prices and reduced global growth pressure; however, conflict-related disruptions to sulphuric acid shipments — a critical refining input — remain an active supply-side risk for Chilean producers.

headline: KLDC HITS 39.35 g/t GOLD Over 16.4m at Ontario's Mirado — Bonanza Shoot in 40m Step-Out, 6 Holes Pending
snippet: Kirkland Lake Discoveries (TSXV: KLDC) returned 39.35 g/t Au over 16.4 metres — including a 1,670 g/t Au bonanza interval — within 50.3 metres of continuous mineralization in a 40-metre step-out at the past-producing Mirado property 20 km southeast of Kirkland Lake, Ontario; six additional holes are pending assay.

headline: MANHATTAN URANIUM Completes Dual Acquisition, Controls 15 Past-Producing US Uranium Mines Under New TSXV Name
snippet: Manhattan Uranium Discovery Corp (TSXV: MANU) completed the acquisitions of Urano Energy and Pegasus Resources on May 7, gaining control of 15 past-producing uranium mines across 25 underexplored US properties covering 25,099 acres; both deals received near-unanimous shareholder approval.
